transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-25
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (AtlasHealth CTO), Priya Nair (AtlasHealth ML Eng), Samir Patel (AtlasHealth Infra), Elena Ruiz (AtlasHealth Procurement)

Summary: quick recap and go/no-go on safe switchover, prioritize model pin, and confirm who owns the fallbacks

[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — bench review, which model to pin, and switchover plan. quick confirm on attendees?
[00:11] Carlos Mendes: yeah this is Carlos. Priya, Samir, Elena also here.
[00:16] Priya Nair: hey, Priya.
[00:18] Samir Patel: Samir here.
[00:20] Maya Chen: awesome. Ravi over to you to run through the numbers.
[00:22] Ravi Patel: cool, thanks. so last week we ran the 5k and 25k micro-benchmarks you gave us; i'll highlight the key deltas. v2.0 (float) had median latency ~110ms, 95th ~310ms, token cost X. v2.1-quant had median ~78ms, 95th ~220ms, token cost ~0.72X. accuracy on your entity extraction eval dropped 0.6 points F1, some small hallucination uptick on long context.
[00:54] Priya Nair: right that matches what we saw in sandbox. our concern is the hallucination on longer discharge summaries, that 0.6 F1 matters.
[01:02] Ravi Patel: understood. the quant variant gives a nice cost/latency saving but slightly worse on corner cases. we added prefix caching and warmed the K-V cache; that reduced cold-starts but you still see spikes when new patient ids come in.
[01:22] Carlos Mendes: question — how deterministic is the K-V cache behavior across restarts? we have strict SLAs.
[01:27] Ravi Patel: good question. kv cache (sorry, K-V) persists for warm instances but if node restarts we rehydrate; Durable cache across pods requires the dedicated config, which we outlined in the doc. there is a small window during failover we saw 200-400ms blip.
[01:45] Maya Chen: and that's where soft fallback policies help — route to a float variant when latency breaches threshold. would that work for you?
[01:52] Priya Nair: possibly, but we need to avoid any step that changes outputs for auditing. if we fallback to a different model we need to flag it in the logs.
[01:59] Ravi Patel: we can add a request header and an audit log entry — we tie it to KMS-protected request ids so it shows up in your audit trail.
[02:08] Samir Patel: on the networking side, can you confirm VPC peering specifics? last time the doc said V P C peering but didn't list routing table adjustments.
[02:16] Ravi Patel: yes, that's on the private deployment guide — we'll send the specific route table and NACL steps. for on-prem the on-ramp needs a NAT and the peering uses private IP ranges; we'll put examples.
[02:27] Carlos Mendes: good. procurement stuff for Elena — anything we should expect on contract level?
[02:31] Elena Ruiz: pricing scenario please, Dedicated reserved vs hosted pay-as-you-go and how credits factor in. also SLA terms for latency and audit retention.
[02:40] Maya Chen: i'll share commercial spreadsheet after the call. it will show committed monthly capacity vs hosted per-token and the modeled monthly bill at your 10M token forecast.
[02:52] Ravi Patel: back to model pinning — proposal is to pin v2.1-quant for production traffic with a shadow float v2.0 for a 48-72 hour period to capture divergences. if divergence rate exceeds 1.5% on critical labels, auto rollback.
[03:08] Priya Nair: what counts as divergence? false positives on named entities or missing diagnoses? we need explicit rules.
[03:15] Ravi Patel: we define rules in the eval harness — entity F1 drop > 0.5 points or hallucination rate increase > 1% on the set triggers alert. we'll share the eval rules.
[03:25] Carlos Mendes: can we have a manual hold? i.e., don't auto rollback during scheduled database maintenance windows.
[03:31] Maya Chen: yes, you can set maintenance windows and disable auto actions. also we can schedule canary traffic percentages.
[03:37] Priya Nair: for the 10k run we want top-1 outputs saved with confidence scores and token-level latencies. can you confirm storage location?
[03:44] Ravi Patel: we'll push the artifacts to your S3 bucket; we need an IAM role from you. that will also include the audit logs.
[03:51] Samir Patel: and the KMS integration — are keys customer-managed or Redwood-managed?
[03:55] Ravi Patel: both options. for the Private deployment you use your CMKs; for Hosted you can bring keys via our gateway if you prefer. there's a short doc.
[04:05] Carlos Mendes: okay, sounds like the immediate ask is verification on accuracy delta and the runbook for safe switchover.
[04:11] Maya Chen: agreed. action items we'll capture.
[04:14] Elena Ruiz: on procurement timeline — if the POC validates we want to start contract talks the week of Dec 8.
[04:20] Maya Chen: noted.
[04:22] Ravi Patel: two small technical notes — 1) with the quant variant we recommend a hybrid KV cache TTL of 30m for your workload to minimize cold K-V fills, 2) add a small traffic shaping during switchover (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%) over one hour.
[04:36] Priya Nair: that ramp looks fine. what about instrumentation for debug traces? can we get per-request trace ids?
[04:42] Ravi Patel: yes, request tracing is available; we can forward to your tracing endpoint or store in S3. it includes model variant, token counts, latency, and any fallback flags.
[04:50] Carlos Mendes: quick note — did anyone run the hallucination root cause on the 3 flagged examples?
[04:55] Priya Nair: i looked at two — seems prompt truncation in long contexts caused missing antecedent info.
[04:59] Ravi Patel: in our test we saw that increasing context window and prefix caching softened the effect; also a small prompt rewrite improved recall. we can help craft a stable prompt.
[05:12] Maya Chen: ok let's recap next steps and owners.
[05:15] Ravi Patel: recap: Priya runs 10k with pinned v2.1, capture outputs and latencies; Ravi prepares switchover + rollback runbook and the eval rules; Maya circulates pricing and updated benchmark sheet and pull request with prompt suggestions.
[05:28] Elena Ruiz: can you include an SLA appendix sample for audit retention?
[05:31] Maya Chen: yes will include.
[05:33] Carlos Mendes: any blockers?
[05:35] Priya Nair: just need the IAM role to push artifacts, we'll try to create it today.
[05:38] Samir Patel: i'll coordinate network changes after the runbook review.
[05:42] Maya Chen: perfect. i'll follow up with links: pilot benchmark spreadsheet (https://redwood.example/pilots/atlashealth-bench-2025-11-25), runbook draft, and the eval harness. expect those by EOD tomorrow.
[05:56] Ravi Patel: thanks all.
[05:58] Meeting end: 15:47 PT

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "K-V" spelled as kv, "VPC" transcribed as V P C in parts, proper nouns sometimes off.

References shared during call:
